name: Sanskar Kendra
key_features: Square museum raised on pilotis and entered from below, planned to grow outward as a spiral.

name: National Gallery of Victoria
key_features: Bluestone box entered through an arch in a water wall, with a hall under a stained-glass ceiling.

name: Torres de Satélite
key_features: Five hollow triangular concrete towers of different heights and colours mark a highway as urban sculpture.

name: Radio City Music Hall
by: Edward Durell Stone and Donald Deskey
key_features: Auditorium ceiling of nested semicircular arches radiates from the stage like a setting sun.

name: Pulitzer Arts Foundation
key_features: Two long concrete bars either side of a shallow water court; the light and reflections change through the day.

name: Supreme Court of Canada Building
key_features: Court building on a bluff above the Ottawa River, just west of Parliament Hill.

name: Singapore Flyer
by: Kisho Kurokawa Architects & Associates with DP Architects
key_features: Observation wheel with 28 air-conditioned capsules mounted outside the rim, and a three-storey terminal.

name: 8 House
key_features: A figure-eight block with a continuous path you can cycle to the top.

name: Alhambra
key_features: A sequence of courtyards, water and pattern, each room opening to the sky.

name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
key_features: A tilted disc roof of glazed louvres lights a terraced reading room behind a granite wall of scripts.

name: Bank of China Tower
key_features: Triangulated megaframe of four corner columns drops a prism at each stage, leaving one at the top.

name: Virgilio Barco Library
key_features: Brick ramps, circular courts and water channels make the library a walkable landscape in the park.

name: Calgary Central Library
key_features: Lens-shaped volume arching over a light-rail line, with hexagonal cladding and a timber-lined atrium.

name: Dipoli
key_features: Copper roofs and rough boulder walls follow the rocky site in a cave-like student union building.

name: METI School
key_features: Earth ground floor with cave-like niches under a light bamboo upper floor of open classrooms.

name: Auditorio de Tenerife
key_features: A white concrete wing curls up and over the hall like a breaking wave.

name: Danish Jewish Museum
key_features: Tilted wooden interior inserted in a royal boathouse, plan based on the word Mitzvah.

name: Church of the Cross
key_features: Brick exterior, white sculpted interior and a tall free-standing bell tower.

name: 21_21 Design Sight
key_features: Roofs folded from long steel plates like a piece of cloth, with most galleries sunk below ground.

name: Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Our Lord
key_features: Wide slab tower with a large glass clock face, above dark brick walls studded with granite blocks.

name: Al-Azhar Park
key_features: A park built on a centuries-old rubble mound, with water gardens and the restored Ayyubid wall at its edge.

name: Deutsche Bank Place
key_features: Service core pushed to one side so column-free office floors open to harbour views.

name: Atatürk Cultural Center
key_features: A rebuilt opera house keeping the aluminium-grid facade, with a red spherical auditorium inside.

name: Auditorium Parco della Musica
key_features: Three beetle-like halls with lead-clad roofs ring an open-air amphitheatre.

name: Al Hamra Tower
key_features: A quarter of each floor is cut away in a spiral, so the stone-clad tower seems to twist and fold.

name: 4 World Trade Center
key_features: Minimal flush glass tower whose parallelogram lower floors become a trapezoid plan higher up.

name: Federal Palace of Switzerland
key_features: Domed central parliament block joins two earlier wings above the Aare, rich in Swiss symbolic art.

name: Yokohama Museum of Art
key_features: A symmetrical stone museum with stepped wings around a central tower over a skylit grand gallery.

name: Shiba Ryotaro Memorial Museum
key_features: A curved concrete and glass hall holds a towering wall of bookshelves beside the writer's house and garden.

name: Art Gallery of Ontario
key_features: A long curved glass-and-Douglas-fir galleria wraps the old museum; a sculptural timber stair spirals up.

name: Herz-Jesu-Kirche
key_features: A glass cube around an inner box of timber louvres, its whole front opening on giant blue glass doors.

name: Akino Fuku Art Museum
key_features: A hand-built hilltop museum of rough plastered walls, timber details and a small lookout tower.

name: Manhattan Municipal Building
key_features: A Beaux-Arts tower straddling a street on a vaulted arch, crowned by a gilded statue.

name: Igrejinha Nossa Senhora de Fátima
key_features: A thin concrete roof shaped like a nun's hat rests on three points over a tiny chapel with tile murals.

name: Chicago Board of Trade Building
key_features: A stepped Art Deco tower closes the end of LaSalle Street, crowned by an aluminium statue of Ceres.

name: Tour de Lille
key_features: An L-shaped office tower straddling Lille Europe station, nicknamed the ski boot.

name: Boston Public Library, McKim Building
key_features: Granite palazzo front of arched windows over the vaulted Bates Hall reading room and an arcaded courtyard.

name: Lappia Hall
key_features: A white theatre and congress hall whose stepped roof profile echoes the fells of Lapland.

name: Berkeley Art Museum (original building)
key_features: Concrete galleries fan out and step down from a central atrium, linked by ramps and cantilevered balconies.

name: Anacleto Angelini Innovation Center
key_features: A solid concrete block with deep-set openings and a hollow core, shielding the offices from sun and glare.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace of Yamoussoukro
key_features: Dome and colonnade modelled on St Peter's in Rome, with walls of stained glass.

name: Atatürk Library
key_features: Concrete library with overhanging upper floors and screens, echoing Ottoman wooden houses.

name: Darat al Funun
key_features: Three 1920s houses and Byzantine ruins on a hillside converted into galleries, studios and gardens.

name: Dominion Tower
key_features: Stacked floor plates shift out over one another around a white skylit atrium of zigzag stairs.

name: Biblioteca Gabriel García Márquez
key_features: Stacked, shifted floors around a top-lit atrium, built in timber and wrapped in vertical metal fins.

name: Scientific Information Centre and Academic Library (CINiBA)
key_features: Seven-storey library clad in red sandstone panels with narrow windows set into the pattern, echoing campus brick.

name: Petroperú Building
key_features: 22-storey brutalist headquarters of the state oil company, won in a 1970s competition, with a helipad on top.

name: City of Justice
by: David Chipperfield Architects, b720 Fermín Vázquez Arquitectos
key_features: Courts in separate tall blocks of tinted concrete in different colours, linked by a shared low base.

name: Aviva Stadium
key_features: Bowl that drops low on one side to spare neighbours' light, wrapped in a rippling skin of clear louvres.

name: Dunelm House
by: Architects' Co-Partnership (Richard Raines, Michael Powers) with Ove Arup
key_features: Students' union cascading down the River Wear bank; one straight inner 'street' stair links its five levels.

name: Boston Government Service Center
by: Paul Rudolph (coordinating architect), with Desmond & Lord and Shepley Bulfinch Richardson and Abbott
key_features: Ribbed 'corduroy' concrete buildings wrapped round a raised plaza, with curving stair towers and deep sunshades.

name: Mikimoto Ginza 2
key_features: Pale pink walls of concrete poured between steel plates carry the floors; irregular windows are cut at random.

name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
key_features: White hall under a blue octagonal roof, raised on two 89-step stairs at the end of a vast square.

name: Hong Kong Design Institute
key_features: A huge rectangular block held seven storeys up on four towers braced by a steel lattice exoskeleton.

name: Casa Sindical
by: Francisco de Asís Cabrero and Rafael Aburto
key_features: Brick office slab with a strict grid of identical windows above a stone portico.

name: Museum of Sydney
key_features: Sandstone-walled museum built over the remains of the first Government House (1788), by a forecourt of poles.

name: Colonnade Bridge (Kolonádový most)
key_features: Streamline Moderne colonnade bridge over the Váh, with glass engravings by Martin Benka; rebuilt and reopened in 1956.

name: Stadio Renato Dall'Ara
key_features: Opened as Stadio Littoriale; stands built into the architecture, later a 1990 steel frame and cantilevered roof.

name: Cambridge University Library
key_features: Academic library with a distinctive front-facing tower, resembling Scott's industrial architecture.

name: Galway Cathedral
key_features: Cathedral with a dome and pillars reflecting Renaissance style, plus rose windows and mosaics.

name: Daily Express Building
key_features: Black façade of Vitrolite and clear glass with chromium strips; lobby by Robert Atkinson.

name: Wollaton Hall
key_features: Elizabethan prodigy house with exuberant decoration, built around a central three-storey hall.

name: Bridgewater Hall
key_features: The concert hall sits on 280 springs to insulate it from external sound.

name: Bradfield Hall
key_features: Academic building on the Agricultural Quadrangle of Cornell University, opened 1969.

name: 140 Broadway
key_features: A 51-storey International Style tower with a smooth black facade and Isamu Noguchi's Cube sculpture at its entrance.

name: Alfonse M. D'Amato United States Courthouse
key_features: Federal courthouse for the Eastern District of New York at 100 Federal Plaza.

name: Allegheny County Courthouse
key_features: Among the finest Romanesque Revival buildings; Richardson called it his "great achievement".

name: Billings Memorial Library
key_features: University of Vermont library, designed to resemble Richardson's Winn Library in Woburn.

name: New York State Cultural Education Center
key_features: Eleven-storey New Formalist building on Empire State Plaza housing the State Museum, Archives and Library.

name: Albuquerque Main Library
by: George Pearl (Stevens, Mallory, Pearl and Campbell)
key_features: Concrete-framed Brutalist library in brown brick; open floors subdivided on 9-ft modules.

name: Centre Block
key_features: Main building on Parliament Hill, holding the House of Commons and Senate chambers.

name: Peace Palace
key_features: Neo-Renaissance courthouse chosen from 216 entries in a 1905 competition; funded by Andrew Carnegie.

name: Scheepvaarthuis
by: Johan van der Mey, with Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer
key_features: Regarded as the first true Amsterdam School building; maritime symbols run through the design.

name: Manila City Hall
key_features: Neoclassical, with a south entrance balcony of three arches on Corinthian columns.

name: J. S. Dorton Arena
key_features: The first structure in the world to use a cable-supported roof.

name: Istanbul Airport
by: Grimshaw Architects, Nordic Office of Architecture, Haptic Architects
key_features: Control tower shaped like a tulip; first-stage terminal covers about 1.44 million square metres.

name: Istanbul Grand Post Office
key_features: Atrium topped by orange and blue glass; 16th-century classical Ottoman ornament throughout.

name: Palace of Happiness
key_features: Neo-Gothic palace raised in nine months as a copy of a French Gothic building.

name: Edificio Lapido (Palacio Lapido)
key_features: Art Deco tower on 18 de Julio Avenue, a National Heritage Site since 1989.

name: Hawa Mahal
key_features: Five-storey pyramid of red and pink sandstone with 953 small latticed jharokha windows.

name: Anna Centenary Library
key_features: Nine-floor library on 8 acres holding 1.2 million books; first library building in Asia with LEED NC Gold.

name: Biswa Bangla Gate (Kolkata Gate)
key_features: 55 m gate: a circular viewing ring carried by two parabolic arches on four legs; about 70 tonnes of steel.

name: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre
key_features: Planetarium on Bijoy Sarani Avenue, Tejgaon, designed by Ali Imam; opened September 2004.

name: Black Star Square
key_features: Parade ground with stands for 30,000 and the Independence Arch, Liberation Day Monument and Black Star Gate.

name: Al-Rifa'i Mosque
key_features: Neo-Mamluk mosque with two minarets and a dome, in stone and marble, facing the Sultan Hassan Mosque.

name: Bank of China Building, Shanghai
key_features: Planned at 34 floors, cut nearly in half after Victor Sassoon insisted nothing beside his tower rise above its spire.

name: Broadway Mansions
key_features: Steel-framed red-brick tower in the stepped skyscraper mode; its plan is said to follow the character for eight.

name: Dallas Hall, Southern Methodist University
key_features: Georgian-style brick hall modelled on Jefferson's University of Virginia and inspired by the Pantheon.

name: Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts
by: Barton Myers (design architect) with HKS Architects
key_features: Orlando's main performing arts venue; the 2,700-seat Walt Disney Theater was co-designed with Artec acousticians.

name: Council House
by: Howlett & Bailey (Jeffrey Howlett and Don Bailey)
key_features: 13-storey modernist council headquarters whose heritage value has been publicly debated.

name: Bauhaus Museum Weimar
key_features: New building for the Weimar Bauhaus collections, opened in April 2019 near the Weimarhallenpark.

name: Jyväskylä City Theatre
key_features: Municipal theatre founded in 1961; the current building dates from 1982.

name: Brooklyn Museum
key_features: Beaux-Arts museum building by McKim, Mead & White, dating to 1897 and expanded several times since.

name: Akita Museum of Art
key_features: A triangular museum by award-winning Tadao Ando, with a triangular skylight and a free-standing staircase.

name: Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health
key_features: Gehry's Las Vegas brain-health centre, opened in 2010 and run by the Cleveland Clinic.

name: Curve (theatre)
key_features: Viñoly's theatre in Leicester's cultural quarter, next to the Athena conference and banqueting centre.

name: 425 Park Avenue
key_features: Foster + Partners' redevelopment of an office tower on Park Avenue, completed in October 2022.

name: Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church
key_features: Wright's late church in Wauwatosa, with a shallow scalloped dome that reinterprets Byzantine forms for today.

name: Didrichsen Art Museum
key_features: A Helsinki art museum of 1965, designed by Viljo Revell.

name: De Doelen
key_features: Concert venue rebuilt in 1966 after the 1934 original was destroyed in 1940; a Rijksmonument since 2015.
